author: reek
body: An impression is one printing of a work. The first impression and the ninth are the same book and different objects, and a colophon that could not tell you which one you were holding would be no use to anyone.

author: reek
body: In a content-addressed repository the work has no impressions -- the bytes are the bytes, and the same bytes are always the same work, however many times they are written down. So an impression here records the ACT of printing rather than the thing printed: who did it, and when. That is a fact about the world, not about the text, and it is the part the hash cannot reach.

author: reek
body: Ordinals in English are irregular for exactly three numbers and regular forever after, which is the sort of thing a book about books ought to get right.
